```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 07_sampling_sampling_distribution
title: >
  Sampling Distribution Probabilities
questions:
  - id: height_mean_63
    type: numeric
    prompt: >
      Look at the 16 possible samples of $n = 2$ from our population of
      four heights. What proportion of those samples have a mean of
      63 inches? Enter a decimal.
    answer: 0.25
    tolerance: 0.001
    explanation: >
      Each of the 16 samples in the table is equally likely. Four have a
      mean of 63: (60, 66), (62, 64), (64, 62), and (66, 60). So the probability
      is $4/16 = .25$. We count (60, 66) and (66, 60) separately because
      they put the first and second observations in a different order.
      Some means occur more often than others, so we can't treat the seven
      possible mean values as equally likely.
```
